title: [CursorBrake] Add push-through resistance and walls at inner monitor edges

proposed_comments.body:
### [P1] Give the merged collection a concrete array type

Building Settings fails with `CsWinRT1032` on this collection expression, which also prevents the Settings unit-test build from completing. `Merge` accepts `IEnumerable<CursorBrakeTextPart>`, so the expression targets a nonmutable interface rather than a concrete collection type; the WinRT source generator rejects that target. Explicitly target an array here while retaining the existing element order and spread:

```suggestion
                return Merge((CursorBrakeTextPart[])[Text(string.Join(" · ", parts) + " · "), .. Parts("CursorBrake_Edges_WallNote", IconOnly(from), IconOnly(to), CrossKeyName)]);
```
proposed_comments.title: Give the merged collection a concrete array type

confidence.rationale: The pinned upstream build reproduces CsWinRT1032; the exact one-line array-target replacement passes the official Settings compile and nonempty CursorBrake-filtered tests. This is a compilation correction, not a physical UI validation claim.
